correctness.rationale: The signal model, noise normalization and squared known-template SNR are explicit. The two-point same-bin probability is (1-d/h)_+, giving the exact phase integral B(T,h) through a nonnegative Fubini argument. Both rational pieces and their derivatives join at h=T. Each derivative has exactly one admissible positive root on its side, with root-location inequalities selecting a unique global optimum for every r>0. Substituting its stationary equations gives the efficiency, 1/3 junction and asymptotics. The included checker passed 3713 finite assertions, separate from the analytic universal proof.

originality.rationale: A literature-led fixed-event, random-grid-phase optimization is mathematically different from field-of-view survey-yield optimizations and fixed-cadence observing plans. Actual published-finding corpus and indexed-publication searches found no equivalent closed-form global optimum; full accessible Macquart primary text was compared by objective and parameter dependence. The new scalar crossover and exact efficiency are not directly implied by the published neighboring claims, though the underlying conditional matched-filter SNR is standard. Historical priority remains provisional, particularly where primary full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: The pulse width T is the intrinsic resolution scale of a transient campaign, while R^2 and νT are independently interpretable detector noise budgets. The exact iff crossover tells an observer whether exposures shorter or longer than an event have maximal expected matched-filter information, rather than relying on a vague sky-dominated heuristic. The sharp 1/3 junction and small/large read-noise limits quantify unavoidable phase-smearing and readout tradeoffs. This is a natural complete design classification under explicit constraints, not an arbitrary parameter slice; it does not claim real-world false-alarm or survey-yield optimality.
